title: Selection persistence across pages holds the elicited contract and announces the running count
asA: operator selecting rows across several pages before running a bulk action
iWant: the selection model to persist my row selections across pagination and announce the running count
soThat: cross-page bulk operations are visible and reversible

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an operator elicited `selectionPersistence=cross-page` (ADR-1804), when the operator selects rows on page 1 and advances to page 2, the previously selected row ids remain in the selection model; a return to page 1 re-renders the checkboxes as checked. The check clicks a row checkbox, advances the page, returns, and asserts the checkbox is still checked.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable with elicited cross-page selection persistence
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator selects rows on page 1 and paginates away and back
acceptanceCriteria.then: the row checkboxes on page 1 remain in the selected state on return

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a running row selection, the surface renders the current count in an accessible location adjacent to the bulk action controls; the count updates when a row is toggled without a full re-render of the surface.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable with at least one row selected
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator toggles a second row
acceptanceCriteria.then: the accessible selection count updates by one without a full page re-render

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the operator did not elicit cross-page persistence (ADR-1804's non-elicited default), the selection resets on pagination; the surface names this behaviour in the accessible copy near the bulk action control so operators are not surprised on advance.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable without cross-page persistence elicited
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator selects rows and paginates away
acceptanceCriteria.then: the selection clears on advance and the accessible copy on the bulk-action region names the per-page-only behaviour
